title: Late-shift score notes — Marceline Reyes (runtime SRE loop)
body:
Quick take: interesting candidate. Marceline has solid low-level runtime instincts (memory/KV cache, batching, OOM mitigation) and a practical bias toward shipping. Felt confident in debugging stories; less confident on product tradeoffs and multi-team rollout coordination. Overall: hire-with-probe (strong IC contributor, needs pairing ramp for cross-team ops).

What stood out (positives):
- Deep practical knowledge of memory mgmt for inference: described a local eviction policy + prioritized KV caching idea to preserve prefix hits under tight GPU memory. Cited an oncall incident where they implemented an early-eviction heuristic that reduced OOMs by ~30% (story had metrics but no perf graphs).
- Solid async batching mental model: explained latency tail tradeoffs and continuous-batching decisions, used good examples (sequence length heterogeneity -> bucketed batching).
- Debugging chops: walked us through a kernel mismatch bug that manifested as nondeterministic tokens; rapid root cause (mismatched dtype cast path) and clear rollforward plan.
- Communicates succinctly under pressure; pauses to check assumptions and writes simple diagrams (hand gestures).

Concerns / red flags:
- Soft on rollout policy / stakeholder coordination: when asked about migrating a model behind a canary, defaulted to “we’ll just test in staging then prod” without describing rollout gating, metrics, rollback criteria, or cross-team comms.
- On-call readiness borderline: several times mentioned relying on senior owner to tune thresholds; good at triage but less comfortable owning long-lived mitigations and SLAs. Not a dealbreaker but would require pairing with SRE first month.
- Limited product/context questions: didn’t ask many clarifying questions about customer impact or inference economics (latency vs cost). Tends to optimize for simple heuristics rather than tuning unit-cost tradeoffs.

Raw interview notes (choppy):
- Loopers: Asha (runtime), Rowan (SRE), Diego (infra). 3x 45m bars + 30m system design.
- Intro: strong systems background (previous: small infra startup; shipped runtime improvements for CPU/GPU mixed clusters).
- Whiteboard SD: design request-routing fallback when cluster at capacity. Good decomposition: capacity tiers, model variants, async queueing. Missed: explicit SLA tiers gating (gold/silver) and experiment instrumentation plan.
- Oncall story: GPU OOM on prod after longer inputs rollout. Marceline triaged with heap dump -> fuzzy on how they tracked exact user queries that triggered worst-case; said logs + sampling but didn't mention distributed tracing use.
- Code question: small Python/CPP hybrid bug. Fixed with incremental tests and reproduced locally. Clean explanation.
- Culture fit: pragmatic, likes small teams, prefers autonomy. Not gung-ho about documentation discipline unless required.

Suggested scorecard commentary (to drop into canonical sheet):
- Strengths: kernel-level debugging, memory/kv-cache intuition, practical batching strategies.
- Weaknesses: product judgment for customer-facing rollouts, end-to-end rollback/instrumentation thinking, less experienced with cross-org runbooks.
- Recommendation: Strong hire (IC) with fast pairing ramp on SRE/operational playbooks. Consider earmarking first 6-8 weeks for: incident handoffs, runbook ownership, and one canary rollout owned end-to-end with mentor.

Suggested immediate next steps (practical):
1) Ask for a short take-home (48–72h): sketch a canary + rollback + instrumentation plan for migrating a large model that increases memory per request by 20%. Focus: metrics to monitor, threshold gating, rollback automation, and runbook steps. Evaluate for product judgment.
2) Reference checks: prioritize manager questions about long-lived mitigation ownership and cross-team coordination. Pull ref for specific incident the candidate mentioned (GPU OOM).
3) If green, propose hire at level L4 (senior IC) but with onboarding charter around oncall + rollout ownership.

Unresolved / follow-ups to ask in async: 
- Exact numbers for the OOM incident: how many nodes affected, what was request distribution, was KV cache disabled/enabled, did they change model quantization?
- Any past work on unit-cost vs latency tradeoffs (did they run experiments comparing tokens/s and cost models)?
- How do they decide when to build an operator vs use feature flags?

Misc links / refs
- Candidate repo excerpt mentioned during loop: github.com/mreyes/runtime-utils (unable to open during call)
- Interview recording: internal link (will attach)
- Related hiring ticket: HIRE-1842 (loop notes in Jira).

Personal notes to self:
- Marceline is the kind of person who will move the needle on immediate infra pain (OOMs, kernel bugs). Not yet a rollout evangelist — we should test product judgment before making final offer.
- If we bring them in, pair with Rowan for first 6 weeks on runbooks and canary frameworks. Put clear success criteria for owning 1 production rollout.

Action items:
- [ ] Send take-home prompt by EOD (assign to Asha)
- [ ] Email refs request (assign to me)
- [ ] Add scorecard + short summary to HIRE-1842 (assign to Diego)

End of notes.
